title: The plugin entity grows up - a dropdown entry, plugin-owned controls, and a plugin a Flow can require
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-553 - Upscalers leave the model picker, as plugins. THIS IS PHASE 1, the mechanism. MPI-579 (LTX Video upscaler) is its first consumer and its proof.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN CARD, AND NOT PART OF MPI-579. The mechanism used to ride on a product card - MPI-506, 'SeedVR2 as three plugins AND the mechanism that lets a plugin contribute a dropdown entry'. SeedVR2 was dropped on 2026-08-16, MPI-506 closed `complete`, and the mechanism died with the product while MPI-507 went on sitting `blocked` on a card that had already closed. Fabio raised the split himself on 2026-08-19 ('If we need to create a card for the updating of plugins to accumulate our implementation, then we should'). A mechanism attached to a product dies when the product is dropped; this card cannot be, because no model choice can invalidate it.

WHAT THE PLUGIN ENTITY IS TODAY. js/data/pluginsRegistry.js, one plugin: `image-describer`. PluginDef is {id, title, description, requiredDeps, operation}. A plugin has NO `installed` flag - its deps ARE its install state, derived by pluginAvailability() and never stored. GC protection is pluginRequiredDepIds(), whose server twin _pluginRequiredDepIds has two call sites in routes/downloadManager.js alongside the _orphanedDepIds sweep. The whole entity was shaped for ONE archetype: a right-click action that owns an encoder and returns text. Everything below is a shape it does not have.

EXTENSION 1 - AN ENTRY IN AN EXISTING DROPDOWN, NOT A NEW DROPDOWN. Fabio, 2026-08-19, correcting the first write-up: 'this is not a drop-down. This is part of the existing drop-down. Upscale in the history workspace already contains a drop-down to choose a model.' That dropdown is js/components/Organisms/MpiToolOptionsUpscale/, shared by the image and video tools through its `kind` prop, and it currently lists `None` plus whatever assets loadAll() returns - it has no plugin awareness at all. A plugin contributes an entry to it. Build the contribution point for BOTH kinds now: phase 2 (MPI-507, PiD into the IMAGE tool) reuses it unchanged, and generalising it later is the build-it-twice failure the umbrella exists to prevent.

EXTENSION 2 - A SELECTED ENTRY CONTRIBUTES ITS OWN CONTROLS. Fabio: 'when selected, it will unlock the necessary UI to operate it.' For the LTX upscaler that is a prompt box plus two sliders; for PiD it is pidVariant / pidResolution / denoise, which its op ALREADY declares - so this is generic from day one, not an LTX special case. The sliders display 0-1 and the real range is hidden: 'The mapping should be occulted from the user, as per usual.' The mechanism owns the hidden-mapping primitive; the actual ranges are the consuming plugin's business.

EXTENSION 3 - A PLUGIN CAN BE REQUIRED BY A FLOW, AND CAN SHARE ITS DEPS WITH A MODEL. Two relationships the entity cannot express today.
  (a) FLOW REQUIRES PLUGIN. Fabio: 'Video Face Detailer will adopt this upscaler that we've built. So the plug-in will be a requirement for it, as it is a flow.' MPI-557 is that Flow. Nothing in PluginDef, flowsRegistry.js or the Flow install path says 'this Flow needs that plugin', so a Flow can currently be installed and run with its plugin absent.
  (b) PLUGIN SHARES DEPS WITH A ModelDef. Fabio guessed it would be 'possibly satisfied if an LTX model is installed' - VERIFIED TRUE ALREADY, 2026-08-19, in the code rather than assumed: `ltx23-spatial-upscaler` is in js/data/modelConstants/assetDeps.js, is already served from R2 (models.cubric.studio), and is already listed in the `dependencies` of BOTH LTX 2.3 tiers in models.js. So there is NO dep entry to author, NO R2 upload, and an LTX user already has every weight - pluginAvailability() derives the plugin to installed with ZERO extra download, for free, today. A user WITHOUT LTX simply installs the plugin's deps like any other plugin - Fabio, 2026-08-19: 'Plug-ins shouldn't differ just because of this or that.' An earlier draft of this card called that an open product question; it is not, and the framing was WITHDRAWN.

GC NEEDS NO WORK, AND THAT WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The first write-up of this card treated 'a dep owned by both a plugin and a ModelDef' as a new case with a sharp edge. It is neither new nor sharp: `qwen3vl-abliterated-clip` is the image-describer's only dep AND sits in both Krea2 tiers' `dependencies` (models.js:686, :802, commented 'shared with the image-describer plugin'), so the case SHIPS TODAY. Deps present because a model installed them derive the plugin to installed for free; deps absent are downloaded under the `plugin:<id>` key with the size already printed on the row; a MODEL uninstall keeps what the plugin still wants, and the plugin's own uninstall releases it through `excludeUninstallId` unless an installed model holds it. tests/plugin-dep-gc.test.cjs already exercises all of it, because the dep it asserts on IS the shared one. So this card writes NO GC code and touches neither routes/downloadManager.js nor the Library row. The LTX upscaler is the same shape with bigger numbers - the only consequence being that a user wanting the disk back uninstalls both, exactly as with Krea2 and the describer today.

VERIFICATION is user-ux and needs a real app - spin your own (npm run app:isolated), never the user's :3000. Confirm an installed plugin appears in the right tool's dropdown and not the other's, that an uninstalled one does not appear, that selecting it reveals its controls, and that a slider at UI 0.5 reaches the value the plugin declares rather than 0.5.
